author: Kyle Cassara
title: In my previous article published last week , I talked about
text:
In my previous article published last week , I talked about some of the factors that should bring Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC (NYSE: TSM ), continued success going forward. Growth in the foundry market, due to the rise of artificial intelligence ("AI") and the Internet of Things ("IoT"), will greatly benefit Taiwan Semiconductor with its large exposure to the market (over 55% of market share). Its partnerships with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA ), Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ) and other companies will be crucial as they enter these markets. 
TSM data by YCharts 
While the future appears bright for TSMC, another question raised was whether shares were currently overpriced, and if it would still be a good time to buy. But with an in-depth look at a discounted cash flow (DCF) model of TSMC, it will help show us where the value is coming from as well as the room for growth, even at current prices. I will go through the assumptions of the model and why they were chosen, derive the value of each share of TSMC as traded on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (TPE), and then convert it to the value of an American depository receipt (ADR), the shares we see as traded on the NYSE.
WACC Using the weighted average cost of capital method is a good way to find a rate to discount the cash flows as it considers the equity and debt construction of TSMC.
